column1: # tools/css/gen-selector-tables.py: what the pinned webref `selectors` data does not say, for every selector it lists and for the extras it
# omits. One row per selector, tab separated:
#  1 name       as webref spells it (":nth-child()", "::part()", "&", ">"), or an extra of this file (E, *, #id, .class, [attr], ns|, " ")
#  3 arg        the grammar of what follows the name: none, ident, type, attr, compound, compound-list, forgiving, real, relative, anb, anb-of,
#               lang, dir, levels, state, idents-comma, part-idents, name-or-star, pt-name, enum:<a,b,...>
#  4 flags      ua (a user action pseudo-class), tree (a pseudo-class that asks the tree: never after ::part()), legacy (a pseudo-element the
#               single-colon spelling of which is still valid), alias=<canonical name>, page (a page selector); "-" for none
#  5 pclass     the pseudo-classes that may follow this pseudo-element: none, user, nontree, or names (user,disabled); "-" for a pseudo-class
#  6 follow     the pseudo-elements that may follow this one, by name without colons; *shadow is every one but ::part() and ::slotted(); "-" none
#  7 state      the GTEXT_CSS_STATE_* bits (without the prefix) a match of it asks the caller for, comma separated, or "-"
#  8 cb         the element callbacks (GTEXT_CSS_ELEMENT_CB_* without the prefix) a match asks for, comma separated, or "-"
#  9 spec       the specificity rule: class, element, id, zero, max, nth, hostfn, slotted, nesting
# 10 dep        what a change of the tree can affect for it (the invalidation summary): name, id, class, attr, state, tree, sibling, first-last,
#               nth, empty, has, lang, dir, logical, column, scope, host, nesting, pseudo
# 11 status     implemented (parsed, serialized, matched), parse-only (parsed and serialized; a match is GTEXT_CSS_E_UNSUPPORTED or never), or
#               unsupported (the selector is invalid, as an unknown one is)
